messages:
maya: Heads-up — partner (AcmeAnalytics) requested raw SIEM exports for a PII-filtered workspace for a 30-day window. They want S3 access + their own ingestion. Thoughts on safe, auditable flow? :lock:

linda: We need the MOU + data processing addendum before anything. Also: no raw PII leaves without redaction and an RBAC approval ticket. Minimum retention we keep copies = 90d for forensics. :page_facing_up:

ryan: Ops idea — generate a timebound export bundle, encrypt with a dedicated KMS key (alias/partners/acme), and hand a presigned S3 URL + short-lived role to the partner. Key grants are scoped to a single export object and revoked after transfer. TTL = 48h for the presigned URL. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

eli: Agree. Add a masking proxy in front of the export so we never write raw PII to S3. Minimal pipeline:
```
log >> mask-service (regex/tokenize) >> sign/encrypt (KMS) >> s3://redwood-partner-exports/acme/<export-id>.tar.gz
```
Mask rules live in repo: infra/log-mask-rules. Masker should emit a checksum and redaction summary to audit log.

maya: Can we do "object-scoped" KMS grants? I remember AWS grants are principal+operation-based. Example command?

ryan: Yep — create-grant + operations: Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. Example: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd1234 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/acme-temp --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey --name "acme-export-4231"
```
Then tag the grant id in the export record and call kms.retire-grant when revoke.

linda: Audit requirements: every export must have 
- ticket id in header
- approved_by (security + legal)
- redaction summary (what fields masked)
- retention policy (auto-delete date)
We also need an immutable audit entry in our SIEM that logs the grant id and presigned url creation (no URLs in logs, just object id).

audit-bot: New export request #4231 created by maya, status=awaiting-legal, approvers=[linda, ops-lead]. (reacted :eyes:)

eli: For Splunk customers who ingest directly, prefer pushing to their HEC behind a locked tunnel rather than giving S3. We can spin up a short-lived HEC token and proxy that applies the same masker. Example HEC flow: token TTL=24h, proxy IP allowlist = acme CIDR.

maya: Concern: partner asked for 30d retention on their side. We need to ensure deletion requests are possible if they ask earlier and we can verify deletion. Is there an audit-friendly delete handshake?

ryan: Implemented before: export record has lifecycle state. To delete: partner calls our API with export-id + signed assertion, we run verification, then S3 delete + kms.retire-grant + write audit tombstone. Tombstone includes who requested, when, and verification token hash. We should require their admin SSO assertion (OIDC) for non-repudiation.

linda: Also add periodic reconciliation: daily job that checks exported objects older than retention and asserts grant revoked + sends report to legal + security. Failures create SEV2.

maya: Nice. Who can take tasks?

ryan: I'll do the KMS grant/retire automation and presigned URL lifecycle (PR to infra/exporter). ETA 2d.

eli: I'll wire up the masker proxy and add redaction summary output. ETA 3d.

linda: I'll draft the required MOU language + ticket template and add compliance checks to the export workflow. ETA 4d.

maya: Great — I'll open the partner ticket, attach export template and compliance checklist, and ping legal. We'll follow up with a short runbook for oncall if anything goes wrong. :white_check_mark:

(continued)
